Social Studies.fw: Washington, D.C. Grades K-12 Social Studies Standards (2023)

std.K.1: Describe the roles and responsibilities of being a part of a family, classroom and local community.
std.K.10: Identify why artifacts are historically important, and describe how artifacts help us learn about the past.
std.1.10: Identify symbols, songs phrases and national holidays that unify the people of the United States and different communities within the United States.
std.1.1: Explain what constitutes a community and describe characteristics of different local and global communities.
std.K.21: Identify geographic characteristics of the local community (e.g., climate, population, landforms, vegetation, culture, industry), and explain how these characteristics shape our interactions with our environment and communities.
std.1.7: Describe how different individuals and groups in a local or global community provide services, uphold rights, and work to promote the common good for all members.
std.1.33: Describe the goods and services that communities need (e.g., grocery stores, transportation, public safety), and identify how they are provided by local government and private businesses.
std.1.21: Construct a simple map of the classroom, school or local community, using cardinal directions, physical features and map symbols.
std.1.18: Compare the features of a city, county, state, country and continent.
std.1.11: Identify community leaders from the past (e.g., George Washington, Abraham Lincoln, Susan B. Anthony, Harriet Tubman, Dolores Huerta, Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Harvey Milk, Wilma Pearl Mankiller, Lee Yick and Liliʻuokalani), and compare how each person created change.
std.2.2: Compare different kinds of maps, with a focus on physical and political maps, and identify key parts of a map (e.g., title, legend or key, scale, compass or cardinal directions).
std.3.34: Identify key leaders and representatives of Washingtonians in the District and national government, and explain the roles and responsibilities of each including but not limited to the mayor and the Congressional representative.
std.2.4: Identify and locate the seven continents and five oceans using maps, and describe major geographic features around the world.
std.1.32: Explain the varied ways that people labor, define the term income, and describe the kinds of work that people do inside and outside of the home.
std.3.4: Describe how different groups have interacted with the environment over time, and compare the ways in which Washingtonians interact with their environment with the ways that individuals in at least two global communities interact with their environment.
std.4.45: Analyze the US Constitution, naming the three branches of government (legislative, executive and judicial), and discuss the concept of checks and balances.
std.3.2: Use cardinal directions, map scales, legends and titles to locate Washington, DC on a map, and identify significant physical features and natural characteristics of the Washington metropolitan area.
std.4.43: Analyze the reasons for the creation of the Constitution.
